record.title: Conjectured formula for the uniformly dense Turán density of stars
record.statement:
For each integer $k$ with $4\le k\le 10$, let $S_k$ denote the star $3$-graph considered in the paper, and let $\pi_{\mathrm{U}}(S_k)$ be its uniformly dense Turán density. **Conjecture for stars.**

$$
\pi_{\mathrm{U}}(S_k)=\frac{k^2-5k+7}{(k-1)^2}\quad\text{for all }4\le k\le 10.
$$

The paper proves the same formula for $k\ge 11$ and, for the related notion represented by $\pi_{\mathrm{V}}$, for $k\ge 5$; the uniformly dense cases $4\le k\le 10$ remain conjectural.
record.source_name: Hao Lin and Wenling Zhou, “Turán density of stars in uniformly dense hypergraphs”, arXiv:2510.12576 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.12576

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2025). “However, determining $\piv(F)$ of a given $3$-graph $F$ is also very challenging. For instance, the conjecture that $\piv(K^{(3)}_4)=1/2$ has remained a open problem in this area since R\"odl proposed a quasi-random construction in 1986.”

record.title: The homological connectivity threshold conjecture for k-fold coverage
record.statement:
Let $B_r^{(k)}$ be the $k$-fold coverage complex on the $d$-dimensional torus, let ${\cal{H}}_{i,r}^{(k)}$ be the event that $H_i(B_s^{(k)})\cong H_i({\mathbb{T}}^d)$ for every $s\geq r$, and let $\Lambda$ be the model's intensity parameter. Let $k\geq 1$ and $0\leq i\leq d-2$, and suppose that $w(n)\rightarrow\infty$ as $n\rightarrow\infty$.

**Homological connectivity threshold conjecture.**

$$
\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{P}({\cal{H}}_{i,r}^{(k)}) = \begin{cases} 1 & \Lambda = \log n + (i+k-2)\log\log n + w(n), \\ 0 & \Lambda = \log n + (i+k-2)\log\log n - w(n). \end{cases}
$$

The preceding corollary gives only an upper bound for these homological connectivity thresholds, while the conjecture is motivated by the homological connectivity results of Bobrowski (2022).
record.source_name: Yohai Reani and Omer Bobrowski, “Sharp Phase Transitions for k-Fold Coverage Using Morse Theory”, arXiv:2510.20329 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.20329

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2025).

record.title: The good-prime congruence for meromorphic modular forms with elliptic-curve poles
record.statement:
Let $C/\mathbb{Q}$ be an elliptic curve with $j(C)\notin\{0,1728\}$, and write

$$
F_{k,C}:=\frac{E_k}{j-j(C)}=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}a_n(F_{k,C})q^n,
$$

where $k\in\{4,6,8,10,14\}$. Let $p$ be a good prime of $C$, with $v_p(j(C))=0=v_p(j(C)-1728)$. **The good-prime congruence.** For all $n\in\mathbb{Z}^+$,

$$
a_{np}(F_{k,C})\equiv a_p(C)^{k-2}a_n(F_{k,C})\pmod p.
$$

The source notes that this is a theorem when $p\geq5$, so the conjectural formulation is solved.
record.source_name: Pengcheng Zhang, “Elliptic curves and Fourier coefficients of meromorphic modular forms”, arXiv:2510.23200 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.23200

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of October 2025); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: The CM magnetic divisibility conjecture for higher-order poles
record.statement:
Let $G_{k,D}^{(r)}$ denote the integral linear combination of $E_k/(j-j(\alpha_D))^i$ for $1\leq i\leq r$ having a pole of order $r$ at the CM point of discriminant $D$. Let $k\in\{4,6,8,10,14\}$, $1\leq r\leq k-1$, and set $r'=\min(r,k-r)$. Let $D<-4$ be a discriminant with class number $1$. **The CM magnetic divisibility conjecture.** The form $G_{k,D}^{(r)}$ is $(r'-1)$-magnetic: for every $n\in\mathbb{Z}^+$,

$$
n^{r'-1}\mid a_n(G_{k,D}^{(r)}).
$$

This predicts systematic divisibility of Fourier coefficients in the CM family; the source presents it as a numerical conjecture and does not establish it in general.
record.source_name: Pengcheng Zhang, “Elliptic curves and Fourier coefficients of meromorphic modular forms”, arXiv:2510.23200 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.23200

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2025).

record.title: The complementary-pole coefficient-product divisibility conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G_{k,D}^{(r)}$ be the CM higher-order-pole forms, let $k\in\{4,6,8,10,14\}$, $1\leq r\leq k-1$, and let $D<-4$ be a discriminant with class number $1$. **The complementary-pole divisibility conjecture.** For every $n\in\mathbb{Z}^+$,

$$
n^{k-2}\mid a_n(G_{k,D}^{(r)})a_n(G_{k,D}^{(k-r)}).
$$

This is a numerical divisibility phenomenon for complementary pole orders in the CM family and remains open.
record.source_name: Pengcheng Zhang, “Elliptic curves and Fourier coefficients of meromorphic modular forms”, arXiv:2510.23200 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.23200

record.title: The 1/3-2/3 conjecture for linear extensions
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a finite poset. For distinct elements $x,y\in P$, define

$$
\delta_{xy}=\min\{\mathbb{P}(x\prec y),\mathbb{P}(y\prec x)\},
$$

and let

$$
\delta(P)=\max_{x\ne y}\delta_{xy},
$$

where the probabilities are taken over a uniformly random linear extension of $P$. **The 1/3-2/3 conjecture.** If $P$ is not a chain, then $\delta(P)\geq 1/3$. This conjecture is motivated by sorting problems; the bound is known to be tight, but the conjectured constant $1/3$ remains unresolved, with the best stated general lower bound being $(5-\sqrt{5})/10$.
record.source_name: Max Aires and Jeff Kahn, “Variance vs. range for linear extensions, and balancing extensions in posets of bounded width”, arXiv:2510.26134 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.26134

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2025).

record.title: The distributivity conjecture for lattices with pure minimal injective coresolutions
record.statement: Let $L$ be a finite lattice, and let $A=KL$ be its incidence algebra. Assume that $A$ has a pure minimal injective coresolution. **Distributivity conjecture.** Then $L$ is distributive. The conjecture is motivated by the relationship between pure minimal injective coresolutions and Auslander regularity, and it has been verified for all finite lattices with at most 10 elements; its general case remains open.
record.source_name: Tal Gottesman, Viktória Klász, Markus Kleinau and Rene Marczinzik, “Pure minimal injective resolutions and perfect modules for lattices”, arXiv:2511.03385 (2025).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.03385

record.title: Mascia–Rinaldo–Romeo primality conjecture for polyomino ideals
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a polyomino, and let $I_{\mathcal{P}}$ be its polyomino ideal. A **zig–zag walk** is the combinatorial configuration defined earlier in the source. The rank of $\mathcal{P}$ is the number of its cells.

**Mascia–Rinaldo–Romeo conjecture.** The following conditions are equivalent:

1. $I_{\mathcal{P}}$ is a prime ideal.
2. $\mathcal{P}$ contains no zig–zag walk.

The equivalence is known for polyominoes of rank at most $14$, based on systematic enumeration and computation. The conjecture asserts that the zig–zag obstruction is the only obstruction to primality in arbitrary rank.
record.source_name: Francesco Navarra and Ayesha Asloob Qureshi, “Recent Advances in the Theory of Polyomino Ideals”, arXiv:2511.22778 (2025).
record.references:

record.title: Navarra–Qureshi–Rinaldo domino-stability conjecture for Gorenstein cell ideals
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a collection of cells, and let $K[\mathcal{P}]$ be its coordinate ring. A collection of cells is **domino-stable** when it has the domino-stability property defined in the source.

**Domino-stability conjecture.** The ring $K[\mathcal{P}]$ is Gorenstein if and only if $\mathcal{P}$ is domino-stable.

Domino stability is known to characterize palindromicity of the switching rook polynomial, and computational evidence proves the Gorenstein conclusion for domino-stable collections of rank at most $10$ and domino-stable polyominoes of rank at most $12$. The conjecture asserts the corresponding Gorenstein characterization for arbitrary collections of cells.
record.source_name: Francesco Navarra and Ayesha Asloob Qureshi, “Recent Advances in the Theory of Polyomino Ideals”, arXiv:2511.22778 (2025).
record.references:

record.title: Sun's classification conjecture for suitable two-variable linear polynomials
record.statement:
Let $P(X,Y,Z,W)\in\mathbb{Z}[X,Y,Z,W]$ be called **suitable** if, for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, there exist $x,y,z,w\in\mathbb{N}$ such that

$$
\begin{cases}
 n=x^2+y^2+z^2+w^2,\\
 P(x,y,z,w)\in\mathcal{S},
\end{cases}
$$

where $\mathcal{S}=\{x^2:x\in\mathbb{Z}\}$. **Sun's classification conjecture.** Let $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}^+$ with $\gcd(a,b)$ square-free and $a\leq b$. Then $aX+bY$ is suitable if and only if

$$
(a,b)=(1,2),(1,3),(1,24).
$$

This conjecture classifies the two-variable linear forms that always occur as a square within a four-square representation of every positive integer. The supplied text does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Hai-Liang Wu and Yue-Feng She, “On restricted sums of four squares and Zhi-Wei Sun's x+24y conjecture”, arXiv:2511.23223 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.23223

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2025).

record.title: Zywina's conjecture on possible adelic indices of non-CM elliptic curves
record.statement:
Let $E$ be a non-CM elliptic curve over $4\mathbb{Q}$, let $G_E$ denote its adelic Galois image, and define the finite set

$$
\mathcal{I}=\left\{2,4,6,8,10,12,16,20,24,30,32,36,40,48,54,60,72,80,84,96,108,112,120,128,144,160,182,192,200,216,220,224,240,288,300,336,360,384,480,504,576,768,864,1152,1200,1296,1536,2736\right\}.
$$

**Zywina's conjecture.** The adelic index satisfies

$$
[\operatorname{GL}_2(\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}):G_E]\in\mathcal{I}.
$$

The conjecture predicts a complete finite list of adelic indices for non-CM elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$. It has been verified for all such curves currently in the LMFDB, but remains unproved in general and is closely connected with Serre's uniformity question.
record.source_name: Kate Finnerty, Tyler Genao, Jacob Mayle and Rakvi, “The possible adelic indices for elliptic curves admitting a rational cyclic isogeny”, arXiv:2512.00652 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.00652

record.title: The optimal linear bound for zero-sum Ramsey numbers of forests
record.statement:
Let $p$ be prime, let $n_p=n(p)$ be a positive integer, and let $F$ be a forest on $n\geq n_p$ vertices such that $p\mid e(F)$. Here $R(F,\mathbb{Z}_p)$ denotes the least order of a complete graph such that every edge-coloring by $\mathbb{Z}_p$ contains a zero-sum copy of $F$. **The optimal forest bound.** For every prime $p$, there is a positive integer $n_p=n(p)$ such that

$$
R(F,\mathbb{Z}_p)\leq n+p-1.
$$

The paper proves the weaker bound $R(F,\mathbb{Z}_p)\leq n+9p-12$ for forests with $n\geq 3p^2-12p+11$, while constructions show that the additive constant cannot be smaller than $p-1$.
record.source_name: Lucas Colucci and Marco D'Emidio, “A linear upper bound on the zero-sum Ramsey number of forests in Z_p”, arXiv:2512.06229 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.06229

record.title: Link–knot defect proportion comparison conjecture
record.statement:
For a prime alternating knot or link $K$, let $\gamma(K)$ denote its crosscap number and let $\Gamma(K)$ denote its unoriented genus. At crossing number $c$, compare the proportions of prime alternating links and knots satisfying $\gamma>\Gamma$.

**Defect proportion comparison conjecture.** For all even $c\geq 4$ and all odd $c\geq 11$, the proportion of $c$-crossing prime alternating links $L$ with $\gamma(L)>\Gamma(L)$ is larger than the proportion of $c$-crossing prime alternating knots $K$ with $\gamma(K)>\Gamma(K)$.

The conjecture is motivated by the heuristic that links have more two-sided state surfaces, together with an observed parity-dependent emergence in the data. Its status is open.
record.source_name: Isaias Bahena, Thomas Kindred and Jason Parsley, “Crosscap numbers of alternating links via state codes”, arXiv:2512.09887 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.09887

record.title: Rational Angle Conjecture for maximal volume ideal polyhedra
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a realizable triangulation of the sphere, and consider the volume-maximizing ideal polyhedron with combinatorial type $\mathcal{T}$. **Rational Angle Conjecture.** All of its dihedral angles have the form

$$
\frac{p\pi}{q}
$$

for integers $p$ and $q$. The optimization problem has no built-in preference for rational angles, and the phenomenon has been verified for the globally maximal configurations with $n=4,\ldots,12$, but remains unproved for every realizable triangulation.
record.source_name: Igor Rivin, “Maximal Volume Ideal Polyhedra and the Arithmetic Angle Phenomenon”, arXiv:2512.10087 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.10087

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2025).

record.title: Uniform boundedness conjecture for the Fourier interpolation basis functions
record.statement:
Let $f_n(x)$ denote the basis functions of the Fourier interpolation considered in the paper, for $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ and $x\ge0$. **Uniform boundedness conjecture.** There exists $C>0$ such that

$$
|f_n(x)|<C
$$

for all $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ and $x\ge0$. This is motivated by numerical computations of the first 10000 basis functions, which found very few values exceeding $1$ in absolute value and none exceeding $2$; no rigorous error bounds are currently provided for the numerical method.
record.source_name: David Berghaus, Andriy Bondarenko, Danylo Radchenko, Kristian Seip and Qihang Sun, “The basis functions of Fourier interpolation”, arXiv:2512.18677 (2025).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.18677

record.title: The universal finite-N N-5 scaling-law conjecture
record.statement: Let $N$ be the number of rotor directions and let $K$ denote the number of distinct one-dimensional solution branches. The numerical exhaustion method and solver resolution are the methods used to isolate these branches. **The universal N-5 scaling-law conjecture.** While $K=N-5$ was definitively observed for $N\in\{6,7,8,9,10\}$, we conjecture that this law holds for all finite $N$. For $N>10$, failure to strictly isolate $K$ branches is attributed to the resolution limit of the numerical methods and solver, rather than to a breakdown of the underlying algebraic structure. This extends the observed empirical relation beyond the tested range, but no proof or higher-precision symbolic verification is supplied.
record.source_name: Antonio Franchi, “The N-5 Scaling Law: Topological Dimensionality Reduction in the Optimal Design of Fully-actuated Multirotors”, arXiv:2512.23619 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.23619

record.title: The nice-knot characterization conjecture
record.statement: Let $K$ be a knot. A knot is **nice** when it admits a braid representative equipped with an inversion datum, as defined in the paper. It is **fibered** when its complement fibers over the circle with fiber a Seifert surface. **Nice-knot characterization conjecture.** A knot $K$ is nice if and only if it is fibered. The paper proves the forward computational evidence for all fibered knots up to 12 crossings and reports no inversion data for non-fibered knots; the equivalence remains open.
record.source_name: Paul Orland, Lara San Martín Suárez, Toby Saunders-A'Court and Josef Svoboda, “Quantum Invariants and Fiberedness”, arXiv:2512.23700 (2026).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.23700

record.title: The modulo-10 Collatz conjecture
record.statement: For a positive integer $n\geq1$, if $n$ is a multiple of $10$, replace it by $n/10$; otherwise, let $r$ be its last digit, replace it by $(12n+8r)/10$, and iterate this process. **Modulo-10 Collatz conjecture.** For every starting integer $n\geq1$, the process eventually reaches $4$ after finitely many iterations. This is the paper's first generalized Collatz example and is presented as a conjecture supported by preliminary computational verification; no proof is supplied.
record.source_name: Abderrahman Bouhamidi, “An Extension of the Collatz Conjecture modulo 2^p+2^q”, arXiv:2601.06208 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.06208

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2026). “The Collatz conjecture has been verified experimentally with computer by many authors.”

record.title: Self-reciprocity conjecture for the partial Hasse polynomials of the double cover of $W_{17}$
record.statement:
Let $\Pi_{17}$ be the double cover of the Teichmüller curve $W_{17}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{H}^2/\mathrm{SL}(\mathcal{O}_{17}\oplus\mathcal{O}^{\vee}_{17})$. For $j\in\{1,2\}$ and every prime $p\ne 2,17$, let $\mathrm{ph}^{\Pi_{17}}_{p,j}(J)$ be the corresponding partial Hasse polynomial, and let $n_{p,j}$ be the degree of $\mathrm{ph}_{p,j}$. **Self-reciprocity conjecture.** The partial Hasse polynomials satisfy

$$
\mathrm{ph}^{\Pi_{17}}_{p,j}(J)=\mathrm{ph}^{\Pi_{17}}_{p,j}(J^{-1})\cdot J^{n_{p,j}}.
$$

The conjecture asserts reciprocal symmetry for the partial Hasse polynomials in the computed degree-two cover of $W_{17}$. The source reports that this property holds in the cases computed and conjectures that it holds in general, but gives no proof or resolution.
record.source_name: Gabriele Bogo and Yingkun Li, “Atkin polynomials for families of abelian varieties with real multiplication”, arXiv:2601.16944 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.16944

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2026).

record.title: Tree isomorphism conjecture for chromatic symmetric functions
record.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be trees, and let $\chi_G(x)$ denote the chromatic symmetric function of $G$. **Tree isomorphism conjecture.** If $G$ and $H$ are non-isomorphic trees, then

$$
\chi_G(x)\neq\chi_H(x).
$$

The conjecture asks whether the chromatic symmetric function distinguishes trees. It has been computationally verified for all trees with at most 29 vertices and for certain classes of trees, but the general statement remains open.
record.source_name: Laura Colmenarejo and Ian Klein, “The Total Chromatic Quasisymmetric Functions of a Graph”, arXiv:2601.23170 (2026).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2019–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1910.11859](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.11859).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.23170

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2026). “Notably, Hikita's proof of the Stanley-Stembridge conjecture does not imply the Shareshian-Wachs conjecture, leaving the latter still open.”

record.title: Miller et al.'s conjecture on infinite square-free digit walks
record.statement:
For a positive integer $N$, define the right-append map by

$$
T_d(N)=10N+d,
$$

where $d\in\{0,1,\dots,9\}$. A positive integer is **square-free** if it is not divisible by any perfect square greater than $1$.

**Miller et al.'s conjecture.** There exists an infinite sequence of square-free integers

$$
\{N_0,N_1,N_2,N_3,\dots\}
$$

and digits $d_{k+1}\in\{0,1,\dots,9\}$ such that

$$
N_{k+1}=10N_k+d_{k+1}
$$

for all $k\geq 0$.

This asks whether one can continue a square-free walk indefinitely by successively appending decimal digits. The question was raised by Miller et al.; despite the result in the paper being previously obtained by Mirsky in 1947, the stated conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Evan Chen, Chris Cummins, Ben Eltschig, Dejan Grubisic, Leopold Haller, Letong Hong, Andranik Kurghinyan, Kenny Lau, Hugh Leather, Seewoo Lee, Aram Markosyan, Ken Ono, Manooshree Patel, Gaurang Pendharkar, Vedant Rathi, Alex Schneidman, Volker Seeker, Shubho Sengupta, Ishan Sinha, Jimmy Xin and Jujian Zhang, “Dead ends in square-free digit walks”, arXiv:2602.05095 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.05095

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2026). “Despite its innocent appearance, this conjecture remains open.”

record.title: Unlikely Newton polygons and Ekedahl–Oort types for abelian covers
record.statement: Let $g \geq 18$, and let $m$ be the least common multiple of the exponents of all of the Galois groups of abelian covers of $\mathbf{P}^1$ branched at three points of genus $g$. **Unlikely-types conjecture.** If $p$ is a prime such that $p \not \equiv 1$ modulo $m$, then there exist abelian covers $X_1$ and $X_2$ of $\mathbf{P}^1$ branched at three points defined over $\overline{\mathbf{F}_p}$ such that $X_1$ has an unlikely Newton polygon and $X_2$ has an unlikely Ekedahl–Oort type. The computational evidence suggests that unlikely Newton polygons and Ekedahl–Oort types occur frequently in this family, but the assertion for every prime satisfying the stated congruence condition remains open.
record.source_name: Darren Schmidt, “Ekedahl-Oort Types and Newton Polygons of Abelian Covers of P^1 Branched at Three Points”, arXiv:2602.07693 (2026).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07693

record.title: Asymptotics for higher moments of random polyhedral cone angles
record.statement:
Let $m(d,k)$ denote the $k$-th moment of the random solid angle associated with the model, and let $d$ tend to infinity while $k$ is fixed. For every fixed $kin \{2,3,\ldots\}$, the constants $c_k$ are positive.

**Higher-moment asymptotics.** For every fixed $k\in \{2,3,\ldots\}$, we have

$$
m(d,k) \sim \frac{c_k}{2^d\cdot d}
$$

as $d\to\infty$, where $c_k>0$ is a constant. In particular, $c_2=1$ and $c_3=(12-\pi^2)/8$, whereas $m(d,1)=2^{-d}$.

This conjecture predicts the scale of all fixed higher moments in high dimension and reflects the contribution of configurations close to linear dependence. Its resolution is not indicated in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Zakhar Kabluchko, “Random Polyhedral Cones I: Distributional Results via Gale Duality”, arXiv:2602.08581 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08581

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2026).

record.title: The optimal Sturm bound conjecture for quasimodular forms
record.statement:
Let $k\geq 1$ be an integer, let $\widetilde{M}_{2k}$ be the space of quasimodular forms of weight $2k$, and let $f\in\widetilde{M}_{2k}$. The Fourier coefficients of $f$ are the coefficients in its $q$-series expansion.

**Optimal Sturm bound conjecture.** The form $f$ is determined uniquely by its first $\dim \widetilde{M}_{2k}$ Fourier coefficients. Furthermore, for every integer $m\geq 2$, the reduction $f\pmod{m}$ is uniquely determined by its first $\dim \widetilde{M}_{2k}$ Fourier coefficients modulo $m$.

Computations for $2\leq k\leq 20$ support the conjecture, which would establish that the theoretically optimal Sturm bound holds for quasimodular forms. The claim remains open in the source.
record.source_name: William Craig, “New Types of Sturm bounds via p-adic transfer methods”, arXiv:2602.10240 (2026).
record.references:

record.title: Monotonicity conjecture for extremal depth-one quasimodular forms
record.statement:
Let $w$ be an even integer with $w \ge 6$ and $w \ne 8,10$, and let $X_{w,1}$ denote the extremal quasimodular form of weight $w$ and depth $1$. **Monotonicity conjecture.** For all even $w \ge 6$ but $w = 8, 10$, the function

$$
t \mapsto t^{w-1} X_{w,1}(it)
$$

is monotone decreasing for $t > 0$. This extends the monotonicity properties proved for several specific weights, but the general assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Seewoo Lee, “Inequalities involving polynomials and quasimodular forms”, arXiv:2602.10536 (2026).

record.title: Hegedüs' conjecture on skew Bollobás systems of projective subspaces
record.statement:
Let $W$ be an $n$-dimensional projective space over an arbitrary field $\mathbb{F}$, and let $\mathcal{P}=\{(A_i,B_i)\}_{i=1}^m$ be a **skew Bollobás system** of projective subspaces of $W$, meaning that

$$
A_i\cap B_i=\emptyset \quad\text{for every }i\in [m],
$$

and

$$
A_i\cap B_j\neq\emptyset \quad\text{for all }1\leq i<j\leq m.
$$

**Hegedüs' conjecture.** Every such system satisfies

$$
m\leq 2^{\,n+1}-2.
$$

Hegedüs proposed this bound in 2015 as a projective-subspace analogue of the skew Bollobás theorem. The supplied source does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Yongjiang Wu, Yongtao Li, Lu Lu and Lihua Feng, “Subspace variations of the weighted skew Bollobás theorem”, arXiv:2603.02698 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.02698

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2026).

record.title: Gallardo–Grekos–Pihko conjecture on three-fold restricted sumsets
record.statement:
Let $n$ be an odd positive integer, let $\mathbb{Z}_n$ be the cyclic group of order $n$, and let $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_n$. Write $3^\wedge A$ for the set of sums of three distinct elements of $A$:

$$
3^\wedge A=\{a_1+a_2+a_3:a_i\in A,\ a_i\ne a_j\text{ for }i\ne j\}.
$$

**Gallardo–Grekos–Pihko conjecture.** There is a constant $c$ such that, whenever

$$
|A|>\frac{2}{5}n+c,
$$

one has

$$
3^\wedge A=\mathbb{Z}_n.
$$

Earlier results establish the conclusion for larger density thresholds, including $|A|>n/2$ for all integers $n\geq12$ except $n=15$, while the stated $2/5$ threshold remains the conjectural target.

record.title: Scale-invariant toy Rota Basis conjecture on circuit-rich pools
record.statement: Let $n$ be the rank, and consider the circuit-rich pool instances generated by the source's recipe. **Scale-invariant toy Rota Basis conjecture.** For $n\in\{5,7,9,11,13\}$ and pool size $\lceil2.2n\rceil$, the evolved scale-aware policy succeeds within $O(n^2)$ steps. More ambitiously, there exists a constant $c>2$ such that for every $n\geq5$, on pools of size $\lceil cn\rceil$ generated by the same recipe, a deterministic de-randomization of the policy succeeds. This is a computationally motivated generalization of the finite-rank experiments; neither the all-$n$ assertion nor the required de-randomization is proved in the supplied text.

record.title: The observable-specific weak-mixing conjecture for phantom gain discrepancies
record.statement:
Let $T$ be the odd-to-odd Syracuse map, let $n_0$ be odd, and let $h_K$ be the phantom gain observable at depth $K$, with reference mean $R(K)$. Define

$$
\eta_K(n_0)=\limsup_{N\to\infty}\left|\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N h_K\bigl(T^i(n_0)\bmod 2^K\bigr)-R(K)\right|.
$$
 **Observable-specific weak-mixing conjecture.** For every odd starting value $n_0$,

$$
\sum_{K\ge3}\eta_K(n_0)<\varepsilon-R\approx0.326.
$$
 This is a weaker, observable-specific target than full total-variation equidistribution and is intended to supply the quantitative error budget needed by the phantom-gain reduction. Its status is open in the paper.

record.title: Non-Parry powers conjecture for roots of $x^d-x-1$
record.statement:
For each integer $d\geq4$, let $4\beta_d4$ be the Perron root of

$$
x^d-x-1=0.
$$

A **Parry number** is a real number greater than $1$ whose greedy expansion of $1$ is eventually periodic; a non-Parry number is a number that is not Parry.

**Non-Parry powers conjecture.** For every $d\geq4$ and every integer $k\geq1$, the power $4\beta_d^k4$ is non-Parry.

The conjecture is supported by computations, and the source remarks that it has been verified up to $d=100$. A proof is not given.

record.title: CMPP conjecture on sequenceability of zero-sum subsets without inverse pairs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an abelian group, and let $A$ be a finite subset of $G\setminus\{0\}$. An ordering $a_1,\ldots,a_{|A|}$ of $A$ is **sequenceable** if its partial sums

$$
p_i=a_1+\cdots+a_i
$$

are pairwise distinct and $p_i\ne 0$ for every $1\leq i\leq |A|-1$. **CMPP conjecture.** Every subset $A\subseteq G\setminus\{0\}$ whose elements sum to zero and such that $\{x,-x\}\not\subset A$ for every $x\in G$ is sequenceable. The conjecture concerns sequenceability in connection with Heffter arrays; the supplied text does not establish its general status, although it proves the claim for zero-sum subsets without inverse pairs of size at most $23$.

record.title: Core-structure conjecture for conditionally non-redundant hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $H=(V,E)$ be a hypergraph of arity $5$ that is conditionally non-redundant for $P_{181}\mid Q_{181}$. For any vertex $v\in V$, let $H_v=(V,E_v)$ be the hypergraph whose hyperedges contain $v$. If $|E_v|=\omega(n)$, then there exists another vertex $u\in V$ such that

$$
(u,v)\subseteq e
$$

for every $e\in E_v$.

**Core-structure conjecture.** Under these hypotheses, every vertex incident with more than linearly many hyperedges shares a second common vertex with all those hyperedges.

This is proposed as an analog of a structural result of Deza, Erdős, and Frankl for hypergraphs with restricted intersection sizes. The source presents the analog as false, so the claim is refuted in the paper's discussion.

record.title: The Piccirillo friend conjecture for twisted Whitehead doubles
record.statement: Let $K$ be a knot with an unknotting crossing $x$, and let $K_x$ denote its **Piccirillo friend**, constructed from $K$ and $x$. A **twisted Whitehead double** is a knot obtained by applying the twisted Whitehead-double construction. **Piccirillo friend conjecture.** The Piccirillo friend $K_x$ of a knot $K$ is isotopic to $K$ if and only if $K$ is a twisted Whitehead double. The paper reports verification for all but $15$ low-crossing-number examples, with the exceptional examples being twist knots and hence twisted Whitehead doubles of the unknot; the general converse remains open.

record.title: Mundici's conjecture on sums of squared Farey gaps
record.statement:
Let $Q$ be an integer greater than $1$, let $S_2(Q)$ denote the sum of the squared distances between consecutive elements of the $Q$-th Farey sequence, and define

$$
C(Q):=\frac{S_2(Q)Q^2}{\log Q}.
$$

**Mundici's conjecture.** One has

$$
C(Q)<3
$$

for all $Q>1$.

This conjecture concerns the normalized sum of squared consecutive spacings in Farey sequences. It was proposed after checking the first $1000$ values of $Q$; the supplied source gives no resolution, so its status remains open.

record.title: Banerjee–Bringmann–Bachraoui's family of congruence conjectures for two-color partition numbers
record.statement:
Let $c(n)$ be defined by

$$
\sum_{n=0}^\infty c(n)q^n=\sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{(-q^{2n+2};q^2)_\infty}{(q^{2n+1};q^2)_\infty^2}q^{2n+1}.
$$

**Banerjee–Bringmann–Bachraoui's conjecture.** For all integers $n$ and $k$,

$$
c\left(2^{2k+3}n+\frac{11\cdot 4^{k}+1}{3}\right)\equiv 0\pmod 4,
$$

$$
c\left(2^{2k+3}n+\frac{17\cdot 4^{k}+1}{3}\right)\equiv 0\pmod 8,
$$

and

$$
c\left(2^{2k+4}n+\frac{38\cdot 4^{k}+1}{3}\right)\equiv 0\pmod 4.
$$

These congruences extend the proposed infinite families of congruences for the limiting two-color partition function. The supplied context does not state that this family has been resolved.

record.title: Non-vanishing conjecture for Pontryagin classes of orientable flat manifolds
record.statement:
Let $\widehat{\mathsf{LS}}_n$ be the orientable flat manifold associated with $\mathsf{LS}_n$, and let $p_i(\widehat{\mathsf{LS}}_n)$ denote its $i$-th Pontryagin class. For a cohomology class with integral coefficients, its **mod $2$ reduction** is its image under reduction of coefficients modulo $2$.

**Pontryagin-class non-vanishing conjecture.** For the orientable flat manifolds $\widehat{\mathsf{LS}}_n$, the mod $2$ reduction of $p_i(\widehat{\mathsf{LS}}_n)$ is non-zero whenever $n\geq 8i$.

The preceding results establish corresponding non-vanishing statements in several cases, including $p_1(\widehat{\mathsf{LS}}_n)$ for $n\geq 8$ and $p_2(\widehat{\mathsf{LS}}_n)$ for $n\geq 16$. The general assertion for all $i$ remains open in the supplied text.

record.title: Abate's weak Wolff–Denjoy conjecture for taut acyclic manifolds
record.statement: Let $\mathscr{X}$ be a taut, acyclic complex manifold, meaning that $H_j(\mathscr{X},\mathbb{Z})=0$ for all $j\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $f\in\operatorname{Hol}(\mathscr{X},\mathscr{X})$. The iterates of $f$ are denoted by $\{f^k\}$. **Abate's weak Wolff–Denjoy conjecture.** The sequence $\{f^k\}$ is compactly divergent if and only if $f$ has no fixed point. This conjecture was disproved by Abate and Heinz in 1992, so the asserted equivalence is false in general.

record.title: Coefficient majorization conjecture for the class $cmathcal{B}_1(\alpha)$
record.statement:
Let $S$ denote the class of normalized univalent functions. For $0\leq\alpha\leq1$, suppose that $g\in S$ has the expansion $g(z)=z+b_2z^2+\cdots$ and satisfies

$$
g'(z)\left[\frac{g(z)}{z}\right]^{\alpha-1}=1+2\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}z^n.
$$

Let $f\in\mathcal{B}_1(\alpha)$ have the normalized expansion referred to as (A-05). **Coefficient majorization conjecture.** For every $n\geq2$,

$$
|a_n|\leq b_n.
$$

The paper presents this as an obvious conjecture in the coefficient problem for $\mathcal{B}_1(\alpha)$, extending known sharp estimates for low-order coefficients and the known $a_5$ bound in a restricted parameter range. Its resolution is not given in the supplied text.

record.title: The pure discrete Morse matching complex simplex-boundary homotopy conjecture
record.statement:
Let $cmathcal{M}_P(K)$ denote the pure complex of discrete Morse matchings of a simplicial complex $K$. Let $cmathrm{cDelta}^n$ be the $n$-simplex and $cmathrm{cpartial}cmathrm{cDelta}^n$ its boundary. **Pure matching complex conjecture.** For all $n cgeq 2$, 

$$
cmathcal{M}_P(cmathrm{cDelta}^n) csimeq cmathcal{M}_P(cmathrm{cpartial}cmathrm{cDelta}^n).
$$

The equivalence holds for $n=3$, where both complexes have homotopy type $cbigvee^{81}S^3$, but the general assertion is presented as a conjectural extension and remains open.

record.title: The effective Linek conjecture for independent sets of trees
record.statement: Let $i(T)$ denote the number of independent sets of a tree $T$. **Effective Linek's Problem.** Every integer greater than $88013$ appears as $i(T)$ for some tree $T$. This is an effective strengthening of Linek's problem, which asks whether infinitely many positive integers fail to occur as the number of independent sets of a tree. The authors report computational verification through $30$ million, but the asserted eventual realization remains open; it contrasts with a conjecture of Han et al. that infinitely many positive integers are not realized by trees.

record.title: The planar Linek conjecture for independent sets
record.statement: Let $i(P)$ denote the number of independent sets of a connected planar graph $P$. **Planar Linek's Problem.** Every positive integer is equal to $i(P)$ for some connected planar graph $P$. The conjecture strengthens the proved result that almost every positive integer is realized by a connected planar graph. record.title: Circulant construction conjecture for doubly saturated $R(3,t)$-good graphs
record.statement:
For odd $t \ge 17$, let $G_t$ be the circulant graph on $5t-10$ vertices whose distance set is

$$
[t-4,t-3] \cup [t+1,(3t-9)/2] \cup \{(3t-5)/2\} \cup \{2t-4\}.
$$

A graph is **doubly saturated $R(3,t)$-good** if it is $R(3,t)$-good and satisfies the paper's double-saturation condition. **Circulant construction conjecture.** The graph $G_t$ is doubly saturated $R(3,t)$-good for every odd $t \ge 17$. This conjecture is based on computer-assisted experimentation and proposes an explicit infinite family; its status is open.

record.title: Universal-constant conjecture for optimal balanced discrepancy
record.statement:
Let $k\geq 4$, and let $\delta^*(k)$ denote the optimal balanced discrepancy for the module-lattice sign-selection problem. Write $\delta^*$ for the constant value proposed by the conjecture. **Universal-constant conjecture.** For all $k\geq 4$, the optimal balanced discrepancy is a universal constant

$$
\delta^*(k)=\delta^*\approx 0.4407,
$$

independent of $k$. The value is supported computationally by certified MILP optimizations for $k\in\{4,\dots,10\}$ and independent local-search verification; its precise number-theoretic identification remains open.

record.title: Woldar's purely singular splitting conjecture
record.statement: Let $k$ be a positive integer and write $S(k)=\{1,2,\dots,k\}$. Let $G$ be a finite abelian group. Say that $S(k)$ **splits** $G$ if there is a subset $T\subseteq G$ such that the translates represented by $S(k)\cdot T$ give $G\setminus\{0\}$, and say that the splitting is **purely singular** if every prime divisor of $|G|$ divides some element of $S(k)$. **Woldar's conjecture.** If $S(k)$ splits a finite abelian group $G$ purely singularly, then $G$ is one of $\mathbb{Z}_1$, $\mathbb{Z}_{k+1}$, or $\mathbb{Z}_{2k+1}$. Woldar proposed this classification in 1995, and it was verified by Hickerson for all $k\leq 3000$; the conjecture concerns the remaining values of $k$.

record.title: Dennin's coefficient-positivity conjecture for Grothendieck pattern coefficients
record.statement:
For $w\in S_n$, let $\Upsilon_w(\beta)$ be the principal specialization of the Grothendieck polynomial and define $c_\emptyset(\beta)=1$ and

$$
c_w(\beta):=\Upsilon_w(\beta)-\sum_{\substack{v\in S_m\\0\leq m<n}}c_v(\beta)p_v(w).
$$

Here $p_v(w)$ counts occurrences of the permutation pattern $v$ in $w$.

**Dennin's conjecture.** For every permutation $w$,

$$
c_w(\beta)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}[\beta].
$$

Equivalently,

$$
\Upsilon_w(\beta)=\sum_v c_v(\beta)p_v(w),\qquad c_v(\beta)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}[\beta].
$$

This is presented as a Grothendieck analogue of Gao's conjecture. The supplied text does not state a general resolution; it records a proof for permutations avoiding the $1423$ pattern.

record.title: Grothendieck inclusion–exclusion positivity conjecture
record.statement:
Let $w\in S_n$ and let $u$ be a subword of $w$. For a word $v$, write $|v|$ for its number of entries and $\operatorname{perm}(v)$ for the permutation with the same relative order as $v$. Let $\Upsilon_x(\beta)$ denote the principal specialization of the Grothendieck polynomial indexed by a permutation $x$.

**Grothendieck inclusion–exclusion positivity conjecture.** For every permutation $w\in S_n$ and every subword $u$ of $w$,

$$
\sum_{u\leq v\leq w}(-1)^{|w|-|v|}\Upsilon_{\operatorname{perm}(v)}(\beta)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}[\beta].
$$

Taking $u=\emptyset$ gives Dennin's coefficient-positivity conjecture. The claim is proved in the supplied paper when $w$ avoids the $1423$ pattern, but its general status is not resolved there.

record.title: The equality of the finite groups \(\mathcal{J}_n^{p,q}\) and \(\mathcal{K}_n^{p,q}\)
record.statement:
Let $p$ and $q$ be the parameters defining the groups $\mathcal{J}_n^{p,q}$ and $\mathcal{K}_n^{p,q}$ associated with the level-$n$ action on the binary tree. The preceding theorem establishes the inclusion $\mathcal{K}_n^{p,q}\subseteq\mathcal{J}_n^{p,q}$.

**Equality conjecture.** For all relevant $n$, $p$, and $q$, one has

$$
\mathcal{J}_n^{p,q}=\mathcal{K}_n^{p,q}.

Computer calculations for $(p,q)=(1,2)$ and $(3,2)$ give matching group orders through $n=12$, motivating the conjectured reverse inclusion. The source provides no proof of the equality.

record.title: Conjecture on the number of distribution-equivalence classes of length-2 mesh patterns
record.statement: Let $p_1$ and $p_2$ be mesh patterns of length $2$. They are equivalent when $s_{n,k}(p_1)=s_{n,k}(p_2)$ for all $n,k\geq0$, where $s_{n,k}(p)$ counts $n$-permutations containing exactly $k$ occurrences of $p$. **Distribution-class conjecture.** There are exactly $105$ equivalence classes with respect to distribution for mesh patterns of length $2$. record.title: The taut 20 conjecture for moduli spaces of stable curves
record.statement:
For the moduli stack $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n}$ of stable curves, let $H^k(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n})$ denote rational singular cohomology, and let the tautological subspace be the subspace generated by tautological classes.

**Taut 20 conjecture.** The cohomology groups

$$
H^k(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n})
$$

are tautological for all even $k\leq20$, and for all $g$ and $n$.

The conjecture extends known tautological-generation results and is attributed in the source to Canning--Larson--Payne. Its bound is sharp because degree-22 cohomology is non-tautological in examples such as $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{2,20}$ and $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{12}$; it remains open.

record.title: Divisor mod-16 equidistribution conjecture for $\Phi_{4p}(2)$
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}_3$ be the prime set used in the paper, let $\Phi_{4p}(2)$ be the cyclotomic value, and let $\omega(N)$ denote the number of distinct prime divisors of $N$. **Divisor mod-16 equidistribution conjecture.** There exists $c>0$ such that for all sufficiently large odd primes $p\in\mathcal{P}_3$,

$$
\#\bigl\{r\mid\Phi_{4p}(2):r\equiv1\pmod{16}\bigr\}\geq c\,\omega\bigl(\Phi_{4p}(2)\bigr),
$$

where $\omega(\Phi_{4p}(2))\to\infty$ as $p\to\infty$.
This is proposed as a more credible divisor-level target than density estimates for primes in a progression. Its status is unresolved in the source.
